item: row 414: the Field data button saves the import's own record (run journals, import reports, the re-index drain's metrics), numbers only
summary: Row 412 found most of a week-long 2M-article import unaccounted for, because the one measured run went into a nearly empty store; the numbers that settle it sit on the import machine and none was in what the Field data button saved. Three GET routes (/api/diagnostics/field-run-journal, /field-import-reports, /field-drain-status) and three button entries after the existing ten. They read the run_logs and import_reports folders and the drain job's in-memory state, never the corpus (the drain status leaves out the backlog count, which is a corpus read). An allowlist projection, not a mask: numbers, booleans, one-word app tokens, ISO times and a few fixed sentences under named keys; every string under a key that names a title, address, path, file, label, message or text is withheld; keys that are not short token-like names are withheld with their value; every kept string and key passes the shared passphrase scrubber; lists over 64 become their length; what was withheld is counted. Each file is cut to 200 KB on the serialised bytes, oldest entries first, and says how many it dropped. The drain now also records its rate against the main file's size in whole GiB, sampled every 5 s inside each call from one stat of one file: the curve row 412's inference rests on (11.6 articles/s into an empty store against 2.1/s on a 41 GB one).
